children: Klook Technology Limited is dropping its plans for an initial public offering.
The online travel company requested to withdraw its registration for an IPO, according to a Friday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
It had initially filed for an IPO of American depositary shares in July 2025.

Klook is the latest company to scrap plans to go public, as higher rates and yields, market volatility, and artificial-intelligence jitters put a damper on what was expected to be a hot fall for IPOs.
OpenAI, Oura, and Australian data-center companies Firmus Grid and Airtrunk are among the firms that have recently postponed IPO plans, according to The Wall Street Journal.
